# Appendix A — Brief and Outline Templates {.unnumbered}

These templates are starting points, not forms to fill without thought. Replace the illustrative text with decisions that a reviewer could use to reject out-of-scope work.

## A.1 Brief template

```markdown
# Editorial brief — [working title]

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Proposed |
| Owner | [one accountable person] |
| Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |

## Reader
[Role, situation and prior knowledge.]

## Promise
[Observable outcome and the evidence that shows the reader reached it.]

## In scope
- [Decision or task]

## Non-goals
- [Attractive adjacent subject] — owned by [artifact or team]

## Evidence
[How claims will be checked: source hierarchy, tests, measurements or review.]

## Change rule
[Release, standard or calendar trigger; what starts a new edition.]

## Assumptions
[What is accepted without evidence and what would invalidate it.]
```

## A.2 Outline template

```markdown
# Outline — [working title]

## Reading path
[What the reader should be able to do at the end.]

## Part I — [question]
### Chapter 1 — [title]
- [Section]
- Exit evidence: [what the reader can decide]

## Part II — [question]
### Chapter 2 — [title]
- [Section]
- Exit evidence: [what the reader can decide]

## Part III — [question]
### Chapter 3 — [title]
- [Section]
- Exit evidence: [what the reader can decide]

## Pilot
[One section, why it is representative and how it will be reviewed.]

## Exclusions
[What this outline deliberately does not cover.]
```

## A.3 Approval block

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Owner | [name] |
| Decision | [approved / changes requested] |
| Date | [YYYY-MM-DD] |
| Evidence | [review record or decision reference] |
